# What is the verified workaround for IsaacLab clearing external wrench for only some envs but affecting all environments?

> **Current answer:** Do not directly call the API with a full-zero tensor and a single env_ids, as the global has_external_wrench may be disabled. A workaround has been tested and verified: maintain a full shape=(num_envs, ...) force/torque buffer, set the target environment row to zero, and call without env_ids. The code modification is proposed to use the updated internal buffer, but it is uncertain in terms of compatibility and not verified by maintainers, so it is only noted as a candidate fix.

## Key terms

- External wrench (external force/torque) (外部力旋量)
- Parallel environment index (environment IDs, env_ids) (并行环境索引)
- Internal buffer (内部缓冲区)
- Global enable flag (全局使能标志)

## Problem and symptoms

- Why does setting zero external force/torque for only resetting env_ids clear external wrenches for all other environments? What is the actual workaround?
- Calling with zero force/torque for env 0 and env_ids results in all non-reset environments having zero external wrench.

## Environment

- Isaac Lab main commit a466d4e; Isaac Sim 5.0; and RigidObject in parallel environments.

## Priority diagnostics

- Distinguish between internal force/torque buffer per environment and the global has_external_wrench switch; check if the second call input is all-zero and if the first dimension of the tensor matches the env_ids.

## Possible causes

- The current implementation sets the global has_external_wrench based on the current input forces.any()/torques.any(), rather than the updated full internal buffer.

## Attempts

- Participants suggest constructing a full num_envs tensor; the author notes that passing a full tensor with a single env_ids leads to shape mismatch and modifies to call without env_ids.
- The author proposes modifying the internal buffer to check _external_force_b/_external_torque_b, but this is not verified for compatibility.

## Effective fixes

- The author explicitly tests and verifies a workaround: retain the full num_envs force/torque buffer, set the target environment row to zero, and call without env_ids.

## Result

- The author confirms that calling with the full buffer and without env_ids works; the local env_ids API semantics are not yet verified for the fix.

## Limitations

- Writing back the full buffer increases data management cost; the source code modification is only a possible fix and not a merged solution.
- The InteractiveScene.reset already resets the buffer, so no additional call is needed.

## Safety notes

- Record actual wrenches for each environment during disturbance or safety recovery testing; do not infer external forces from call parameters alone.
